title: A Monsoon for the Summit
premise: Hazel Reyes, a disgraced storm chaser hiding in a coastal town from the syndicate he owes, is dragged back into the field when his old rival, Ingrid Voss, hires his ragtag crew to escort a climatologist up a remote Himalayan-adjacent ridge before monsoon season locks the passes. The job is supposed to be simple logistics, but the scientist is secretly chasing evidence of a weather phenomenon the expedition's backers will kill to control—and Hazel recognizes the ridge as the site of the disaster that ended his career and cost his brother's life. As the debt collectors close in and the monsoon advances, Hazel must choose between erasing the evidence to protect his found family or exposing a truth that will destroy the man who saved him. He brings everyone home alive, burns the data, and finally pays his debt—not in money, but by surrendering the legend he built his invisibility on.
about_author: M. M. Crane is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent a decade outfitting scientific teams in monsoon-belt mountain ranges before turning to fiction. They write from a small harbor town, where they still keep a barometer on the porch and refuse to predict anything with confidence.

chapters.title: The Weight of Fair Weather
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the port town of Salagdan, Hazel dodges a debt collector's polite threat, patching radar units and keeping his storm-chasing crew—mechanic Dev, navigator June, and rookie Teo—deliberately underemployed. The emotional beat is the exhausting vigilance of a man pretending his past is finished. It ends with Ingrid Voss walking into his workshop, smiling, holding a contract he can't afford to refuse.

chapters.title: Terms Written in Rain
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Ingrid offers triple pay to guide climatologist Dr. Ansel Brandt up the Kirat Ridge before the monsoon—sworn-off territory where Hazel's brother died nine years ago. Hazel negotiates brutally, telling himself it's about the debt. The beat is self-deception: he signs not for money but because refusing would mean admitting the ridge still owns him. June reads him instantly and says nothing, which is worse.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The expedition assembles at the trailhead: sealed instrument cases Ansel won't explain, and a tension between him and Ingrid that predates the crew. Teo idolizes Ansel; Hazel watches the scientist's hands shake whenever the ridge comes into view. The beat is unease dressed as professionalism. Ansel's chapter reveals he's lying to his own backers about what the instruments are for—and that he knows Hazel's real name.

chapters.title: The Pass Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Three days up, the crew crosses the old base-camp site of the 2016 disaster. Dev finds a rusted carabiner stamped with Hazel's brother's initials and quietly pockets it. The emotional beat is grief surfacing through competence—Hazel navigates flawlessly while coming apart inside. That night, Ingrid admits she chose him deliberately: she needs someone who knows what the ridge took.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Sing
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. At high camp, Teo helps Ansel deploy the sensors and accidentally glimpses the data: a recurring pressure signature suggesting the ridge generates a predictable storm cell—a weaponizable weather key. Teo, hungry to belong, promises to keep the secret, and feels the crew's trust curdle into complicity. The beat is the intoxication and dread of being trusted with something too big.

chapters.title: Optimists at the Door
chapters.summary: June's POV. A satellite call: the syndicate has found the expedition and is inbound with two of Ingrid's former backers, who want the data as payment for everyone's debts. June realizes the job was never a job—it was bait, and Ingrid may be running her own con. The beat is betrayal and loyalty colliding; June starts planning contingencies without telling Hazel, protecting him the way he's protected all of them.

chapters.title: Whiteout Terms
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The monsoon arrives early, a full day ahead of forecast—the ridge's signature storm, exactly as Ansel's data predicted. The crew is pinned above the icefall with the collectors two valleys behind. The beat is terror transmuted into clarity: Hazel realizes the storm isn't the obstacle, it's the proof, and whoever controls the forecast controls the mountain. He makes a plan he doesn't share with Ingrid.

chapters.title: The Descent Bargain
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Cornered at the icefall, Ingrid offers the collectors Ansel's drives in exchange for clearing the debt—then watches Hazel sabotage the handoff, triggering a controlled avalanche that buries the syndicate's route and forces a unified descent. The beat is Ingrid's reckoning: she engineered this to reclaim her reputation and instead witnesses Hazel choose his crew over his survival. Ansel, wounded, calls him a fool.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The climax: during the final storm crossing, Ansel tries to broadcast the data to his backers and Hazel stops him—not with violence but with the truth about his brother, who died because a previous team monetized a forecast and lied about the risk. Ansel, broken open, hands over the drives. Hazel drops them into a crevasse as the monsoon swallows the ridge. The beat is grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: A Monsoon for the Summit
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Weeks later in Salagdan, the crew is poorer, debt-free through Ingrid's quietly settled accounts, and publicly ridiculed for a failed expedition. Teo, now trusted with real responsibility, watches Hazel repair radar units with steady hands and the carabiner hung above his bench. The beat is belonging without absolution: the mountain kept its secret, the family kept each other, and for the first time Hazel isn't waiting for the next storm to define him.
